newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi market depressed despite good trading.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi market depressed despite good trading.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) market was on average still depressed on Thursday despite the sale at a premium of National Industrial Credit shares on the three-day special lots board, brokers said.
The index fell 16.18 points to 3036.94 while turnover rose to 236.121 million shillings on 5,499,434 shares from 6.430 million shillings on 208,703 shares on Wednesday.

National Industrial Credit was the most heavily traded counter. Barclays Bank of Kenya sold 11 percent of its shareholding in National Industrial Credit -- some 4.8 million shares -- at 45 shillings, down from the 52-shilling price it had offered it at.
But this price was still at a premium from NIC's market price of around 40 shillings, provoking complaints from other shareholders.
The buyer was the Insurance Company of East Africa (ICEA), which is not listed on the Nairobi Stock Exchange.
National Industrial Credit announced a dividend of 1.50 shillings.

"The new buyer has got to maintain investor confidence and will therefore maintain the dividend at the same price," a broker told Reuters, saying previous confidence in was derived from Barclays' role its its ownership.
But brokers said the market would continue bearish because of a lack of investor confidence added to the sudden influx of shares from troubled financial institutions under liquidation.
The market ignored a strike called by pilots employed by national carrier Kenya Airways which has meant the cancellation of a number of flights since Wednesday.
Kenya Airways traded 73,170 shares at 9.80 from 9.90.
Kenya Commercial Bank rose to 52.50 from 52.
Firestone East Africa dealt 490,100 shares unchanged at 28, Kenya Power & Lighting fell 1.0 to 116 from 117 and Bamburi Cement eased to 28.50 from 30.
Bourse officials said that foreign investors dealt 90,000 shares of Firestone East Africa at 28 and 3,997 shares of Diamond Trust at 38 from 38.50.
